enum.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_CLASS
enum.description: Classification of a target across physical and non-physical domains.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_CLASS_MINE
entry.description: Naval mine or underwater explosive hazard.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_CLASS_DEPOT
entry.description: Depot, storage site, or logistics node.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_DOMAIN_CYBER

enum.description: Target entity class, representative subset of the MIL-STD-2525D (Distribution A) land entity library. Note 2525D has no separate IFV entity; an IFV renders as ARMORED_FIGHTING_VEHICLE. Pin the 2525D version to the target 6017 baseline for lossless round-trip.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ENT_EW_MI

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_PACKAGE_TRANSPORT_UNKNOWN

entry.description: Authorization is required before action can be taken.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_FLAG_GNSS_DEGRADED
entry.description: GNSS quality was degraded when the target was generated.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_FLAG_LINK_DEGRADED
entry.description: Link quality was degraded when the target was generated.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_FLAG_MOVING
entry.description: Target is assessed to be moving.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_FLAG_INTEGRITY_PRESENT
entry.description: Associated target package contains integrity material.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_FLAG_MANUAL_DESIGNATION
entry.description: Target was designated manually by an operator.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_FLAG_AUTONOMOUS_DETECTION
entry.description: Target was detected or designated autonomously.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_SENSOR_TYPE
enum.description: Primary sensor source used for target identification.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_SENSOR_TYPE_UNKNOWN
entry.description: Unknown or unspecified target identification sensor.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TARGET_SENSOR_TYPE_FUSED
entry.description: Multiple sensor sources were fused for target identification.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_TAC_TYPE
enum.description: Type of terminal attack control, a defined construct in JP 3-09.3 (Close Air Support). The three types are distinguished by what the terminal controller can visually acquire before granting clearance.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TAC_TYPE_1
entry.description: Type 1: controller must visually acquire both the attacking aircraft and the target before clearance.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TAC_TYPE_2
entry.description: Type 2: controller clears an individual attack without visually acquiring the aircraft and/or target at release.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TAC_TYPE_3
entry.description: Type 3: controller grants clearance for multiple attacks within a defined engagement/period under stated restrictions.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_CAS_CLEARANCE
enum.description: CAS clearance / abort handshake verbs (JP 3-09.3). Human-authority instruments.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_AIRCRAFT_CALL
enum.description: Attacking-aircraft status calls (JFIRE 9-line flow).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MARK_TYPE
enum.description: Type of target mark / terminal guidance (9-line line 7).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MARK_LASER
entry.description: Laser designation (code carried as slot, not value).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_ORDNANCE_DELIVERY
enum.description: Bomb-on-coordinate vs bomb-on-target delivery intent.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATUS
enum.description: Sequential lifecycle of a fitted payload, common to ESAD, gun, and non-lethal classes. States are mutually exclusive and progress in order. Replaces the previous ESAD arming / munition / ignition state triad. Each state carries at most one auxiliary datum (payload_aux on PAYLOAD_STATE); the aux meaning is defined by the state it is reported with, so an observer never has to disambiguate a countdown from an error code from an environmental reading.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_NOT_PRESENT
entry.description: Payload not detected in the store. payload_aux: none (0).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_IDLE
entry.description: Detected and locally safe — for an ESAD this is the safety pin present or trigger lock engaged (formerly PIN_PRESENT plus ARMING_DISARMED). payload_aux: none (0), or an environmental-condition code (implementation-defined) if the safe/lockout is environmental.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SST
entry.description: In the safe-separation lockout, counting down from a defined timer value. payload_aux: remaining seconds (string).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DISARMED
entry.description: Detected and cleared to arm on request. payload_aux: none (0).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_ARMING
entry.description: Actively attempting to arm (handshake / self-test in flight). payload_aux: none (0).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_ARMED
entry.description: Armed and ready for activation. payload_aux: none (0).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_ACTIVATED
entry.description: Activation function has executed (gun: fired; ESAD: detonated; non-lethal: round cycled). payload_aux: none (0).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DISABLING
entry.description: Actively attempting to disable / render safe. payload_aux: none (0).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DISABLED
entry.description: Disabled; requires power cycle or service to function again. payload_aux: none (0).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_ERROR
entry.description: Payload experienced an internal or subsystem error. payload_aux: error descriptor code (implementation-defined), or 0 if none.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATUS_FLAGS
enum.description: Condition flags on payload state telemetry. Multiple bits may be set at once; consumers gate on a bit test. Mirrors the MIL-STD-1553 status word, which sets multiple condition flags (Busy, Subsystem Flag, Terminal Flag, Service Request) simultaneously. Distinct from the state-bound payload_aux: the flags say which conditions hold, the aux carries the human-meaningful detail of the current state.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FLAG_BUSY
entry.description: An actuation is in progress (arming, disarming, activating, deactivating). 1553 Busy analog.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FLAG_FAULT_SUBSYSTEM
entry.description: A payload-subsystem fault is active — sensor gating, power, fuze or other dependency. 1553 Subsystem Flag analog.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FLAG_FAULT_INTERNAL
entry.description: A payload-internal error is active, distinct from a subsystem fault. 1553 Terminal Flag analog.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FLAG_SERVICE_REQUEST
entry.description: The payload requests a service (e.g. a self-test result, a configuration acknowledgement). 1553 Service Request analog.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FLAG_SENSOR_GATED
entry.description: At least one required sensor is not reporting health = OK on this payload; arming / activation will be blocked. See required_sensor_mask on PAYLOAD_SETTINGS for the readiness recipe.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FLAG_FIRED
entry.description: Activation has fired and the state machine has advanced (payload class where the actuation is a one-shot: ESAD detonation, gun round flight, non-lethal round cycled). Set on the state report following ACTIVATE; cleared on the next report.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATE_CHANGE_REQUEST
enum.description: Requested lifecycle transition for a payload. ACTIVATE is a one-shot capability execution (fire, detonate, cycle), not a persistent state; modeled on MIL-STD-1553 mode codes. MODE is valid only together with the mode_change field on the same message. Disarm and deactivate always apply; arm and activate require the carrier's release consent (STORE_STATUS.release_consent = 1) on the targeted bay.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATE_CHANGE_REQUEST_NONE
entry.description: No state change requested. Two-state zero-action per the dialect enum rule: a zero-filled control message is a valid no-op, not an arm.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATE_CHANGE_REQUEST_MODE
entry.description: Request mode change; the selected mode is carried in mode_change.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATE_CHANGE_REQUEST_ACTIVATE
entry.description: Request activation of the payload function (one-shot).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATE_CHANGE_REQUEST_DEACTIVATE
entry.description: Request deactivation of the active function without a full disarm.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FUNC_TYPE
enum.description: Payload capability - what the device does. Shared by PAYLOAD_STATE (report of the fitted capability) and PAYLOAD_CONTROL.mode_change (commanded mode when state_change = MODE).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FUNC_TYPE_NONE
entry.description: Capability unspecified / no function mode selected.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FUNC_TYPE_COMMAND
entry.description: Commanded function: acts only on explicit operator command (gun semi, manual actuation).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FUNC_TYPE_PROXIMITY
entry.description: Proximity function: acts automatically inside a device-defined standoff (ESAD proximity mode). The coarse detent the device holds is reported on PAYLOAD_SETTINGS.act_dist and must never be widened to a continuous value on the wire.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FUNC_TYPE_SEMI_AUTO
entry.description: Semi-automatic function: one round per operator trigger, sensor-assisted release window.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FUNC_TYPE_EXPLOIT
entry.description: Exploit function for a specific capability (e.g. loitering munition attack run).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_FUNC_TYPE_DROP
entry.description: Drop function (gravity release; the carrier performs the actuation).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CONFIG
enum.description: Category of one config pair in a PAYLOAD_CONFIG partial update. Values are category-native: WEIGHT → config_value in grams; PAYLOAD_ID / STORE_ID → numeric id in config_value. The assigned name is carried in the separate config_name field. This is a closed set: a setting is settable only if a category exists for it.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CONFIG_PAYLOAD_ID
entry.description: Assign / change the payload instance id.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CONFIG_STORE_ID
entry.description: Assign / change the carrier slot id.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CONFIG_WEIGHT
entry.description: Payload mass assigned in the carrier's record (config_value in grams).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CLASS
enum.description: Payload function class, so a consumer that knows only this dialect can interpret the sensor subset and payload_aux meanings normative for the fitted device. One byte on PAYLOAD_STATE and PAYLOAD_SENSOR_STATUS; required non-UNKNOWN whenever class-banded fields are present. The model is the MIL-STD-3014 CLASS CODE: a registered identifier whose meaning is resolved against the registered per-class entries (descriptors), not inline in the value. UNKNOWN consumers MUST treat class-banded sensor entries as implementation-defined and display them verbatim.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CLASS_NON_LETHAL
entry.description: Non-lethal capability class (flare, chaff, laser, etc.).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CLASS_LOITERING
entry.description: Loitering munition / one-way-attack class. The consent handshake for this class stays on LOITER_MUNITION_CONTROL (53036) and is not folded into PAYLOAD_CONTROL.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DATA_KIND
enum.description: How a sensor status value must be read. Prevents value/min/max overloading on discrete or count-type readings (e.g. a breech state riding value/min/max as a 0..1 range, or a remaining-rounds count where max = loaded and min = 0 is not a valid operating window). 0 = unknown, so a zero-filled field never decodes as a substantive default.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DATA_KIND_ANALOG
entry.description: Continuous reading; value in sensor units, value_min / value_max the valid operating window.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DATA_KIND_COUNT
entry.description: Remaining quantity (ammo, flares, chaff); value = integer count, min = zero, max = loaded.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DATA_KIND_DISCRETE
entry.description: Two-or-few states (breech open/closed, lock engaged); value = state number per the sensor_type definition; min = 0, max = highest defined state.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_DATA_KIND_TEXT
entry.description: Symbolic reading; value is an index into an implementation-defined label set, rendered verbatim by consumers.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SENSOR_TYPE
enum.description: Sensor type feeding a payload's gating / status system. Replaces the decel-scoped STORE_SENSOR_TYPE allocation with a class-wide one: shared entries (canonical, used by multiple classes) have the low values; class-band entries are grouped per class (decel / landing, gun, non-lethal) so class-specific types have a home without a side table. The band ceiling is the hard limit - the readiness bitmask on PAYLOAD_SETTINGS is uint32_t, so the total set of sensor types a carrier can ever gate must stay at or below 32; plan the allocation deliberately. Consumers MUST treat unknown values as "sensor present; class not recognized" and may use health for gating decisions. The model is the MIL-STD-3014 CLASS CODE + DESCRIPTOR pattern: the sensor type entry is the descriptor; the payload_class field on the message resolves which descriptor applies for a class-banded value.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SENSOR_VOLTAGE
entry.description: Supply voltage / battery state of the device.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SENSOR_MECH_STATE
entry.description: Generic mechanical state (lock engaged/released, round cycled).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SENSOR_GUN_ROUNDS_READY
entry.description: Rounds loaded and available (gun class). KIND=COUNT.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_RWS_ARMING_STATE
enum.description: Remote weapon system arming state.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MATCH_MEDIA_TYPE
enum.description: Media type used for target matching.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_DEVIATION
enum.description: Deviation spotting relative to the observer-target (OT) line (ATP 3-09.30 / VMF K02.22).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_DEVIATION_LINE
entry.description: Impact on the OT line; zero lateral deviation.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_DEVIATION_LEFT
entry.description: Impact left of the OT line (correction: shift right).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_DEVIATION_RIGHT
entry.description: Impact right of the OT line (correction: shift left).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE
enum.description: Range spotting along the observer-target line (ATP 3-09.30 / STANAG 1034 / VMF K02.22).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_OVER
entry.description: Impact beyond the target (range too long; decrease range).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_SHORT
entry.description: Impact between observer and target (range too short; increase range).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_TARGET
entry.description: Direct hit at target range (precision/registration); enter fire for effect.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_RANGE_CORRECT
entry.description: Impact at correct range along the OT line.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_STRADDLE
entry.description: Multi-gun salvo: rounds fell both over and short; MPI correct, enter FFE.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_DOUBTFUL
entry.description: Impact seen but cannot be called over/short.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_UNOBSERVED
entry.description: Heard/seen but cannot determine over/short (distinct from LOST).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_RANGE_NEGLECT
entry.description: Naval (NSFS): last salvo fired on incorrect data; disregard spotting.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_HOB
enum.description: Height-of-burst spotting (ATP 3-09.30). An OBSERVATION of where the round detonated vertically, NOT a munition property or a fuze setting. Drives the doctrinal vertical correction (e.g. graze on an intended airburst => "Up 40").

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_HOB_AIR
entry.description: Detonated in the air as intended.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_HOB_GRAZE
entry.description: Detonated on contact with the ground (ground-burst).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_HOB_MIXED
entry.description: Salvo: air and graze bursts, no clear majority.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_HOB_RIPPED_CHUTE
entry.description: Illumination parachute ripped/separated on deployment; repeat illum.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_HOB_DARK_STAR
entry.description: Illumination round failed to deploy or properly ignite (ATP 3-09.32).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_SURFACE
enum.description: Supplementary: what the round struck / what the splash was observed in/on. Sensor context, not part of the doctrinal spotting set.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_SURFACE_WATER
entry.description: Water surface. A near-miss beside a vessel reports this.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_SURFACE_VEHICLE
entry.description: Land vehicle (tank, IFV, truck). Mobile; may have moved by next correction.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_SURFACE_SURFACE_VESSEL
entry.description: Ship or boat. Distinct from WATER so hit-vs-near-miss on a vessel is unambiguous.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_SURFACE_FOLIAGE
entry.description: Tree canopy / vegetation; may cause early function or masking.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_OBSCURATION
enum.description: Supplementary: why the observer could not fully resolve the impact. Relates to RANGE_DOUBTFUL / RANGE_LOST.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_OBSCURATION_SMOKE
entry.description: Masked by smoke or dust (own or battlefield).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_OBSCURATION_WEATHER
entry.description: Masked by cloud, fog, or precipitation.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_OBSCURATION_SENSOR_LIMIT
entry.description: Sensor resolution / range / angle limit, not an external mask.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_FIRE_MISSION_COMMAND
enum.description: Procedural fire-mission control commands exchanged in the observer/FDC digital handshake (ATP 3-09.30; map to VMF K02.16 End of Mission and K02.22 Subsequent Adjust flows). These are control verbs, not spotting.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FMC_RECORD_AS_TARGET
entry.description: Record the current data as a target.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FMC_FRESH_TARGET
entry.description: Fresh target: interrupt current mission for higher-priority target (NSFS).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FMC_NEW_TARGET
entry.description: New target: engage additional non-priority target, continue original (NSFS).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MUNITION_CLASS
enum.description: Projectile / shell class for the call-for-fire method of engagement (ATP 3-09.30 element 5). The projectile is a distinct component from the fuze; the two are specified separately. This is requester intent, not weaponeering configuration.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_FUZE_MODE
enum.description: Requested fuze MODE for the call-for-fire method of engagement (ATP 3-09.30). Product-independent: selects the standard fuze behavior category (the observer's intent), NOT internal fuze timing or height-of-burst settings, which remain device-internal and out of scope. Whether the fielded fuze is multi-option (e.g. M782 MOFA) is carried separately as the fuze_mofa_capable flag on FIRES, since MOFA is a capability, not a mode.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FUZE_MODE_DELAY
entry.description: Delay; detonate after impact for penetration.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FUZE_MODE_TIME
entry.description: Mechanical/electronic time; burst at a set point in trajectory.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FUZE_MODE_VT
entry.description: Variable time / proximity; burst at a preset height above ground.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_HOB_INTENT
enum.description: Descriptive airburst height-of-burst intent for proximity/time modes. A selector, NOT a millisecond or metric value.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_CUE_TYPE
enum.description: Intent of a non-kinetic point-of-interest cue. These values explicitly denote observation/investigation tasking and carry NO engagement semantics. A consumer must not interpret a TARGET_CUE as a fires order.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_CUE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
entry.description: Not specified (default for an unset field). A consumer must not act on an unspecified cue type.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_CUE_TYPE_INVESTIGATE
entry.description: Proceed to the point and gather further information. Non-kinetic.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_CUE_TYPE_OBSERVE
entry.description: Maintain standoff observation of the point. Non-kinetic.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_CUE_TYPE_MARK
entry.description: Record/mark the point as a reference of interest. No tasking implied.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_RESULT
enum.description: Result of receiving/processing a MAVLink-M message, reported via MAVLINK_M_ACK. Distinguishes "received" from "accepted" so a sender can tell delivery from agreement.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_RECEIVED
entry.description: Message was received and parsed. No acceptance implied.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_ACCEPTED
entry.description: Message was received and accepted/actioned by the recipient.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_REJECTED
entry.description: Message was received but rejected (e.g. operator declined the cue).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_UNSUPPORTED
entry.description: Message type or requested action is not supported by the recipient.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_FAILED
entry.description: Message was received but processing failed (e.g. malformed or stale, or a start (SAFETY BOUNDARIES) dated later than the receiving system's clock plus the maximum clock offset).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_EXPIRED
entry.description: Message was received after its validity window had passed: a start (SAFETY BOUNDARIES) whose time_usec is older than the maximum age the receiving system is configured with. A stop is never rejected for its time.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_NOT_APPLICABLE
entry.description: Message was addressed to this system, and nothing on this system is what it applies to, for example a stop for an engagement this system does not hold. A final result. Never sent in answer to a message sent to every system: a system where such a message selects nothing does not answer it.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_HELD
entry.description: A start (SAFETY BOUNDARIES) was not applied because it may have been issued before a stop the receiving system recorded and that covers it, or before the system restarted. It may be the start the stop was sent to prevent, so it is issued again, with a new time_usec, only as a new decision of its authority, never automatically. A final result.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK_NO_TIME
entry.description: The receiving system cannot keep its clock within half the maximum clock offset of UTC, so it rejects every start (SAFETY BOUNDARIES) and acts only on stops until it can. A final result.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_HEALTH
enum.description: Health state of an individual store sensor.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_HEALTH_DEGRADED
entry.description: Sensor functional but degraded (e.g. noisy, low confidence).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_HEALTH_CALIBRATING
entry.description: Sensor initializing or calibrating; not yet usable.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_HEALTH_OUT_OF_RANGE
entry.description: Sensor reading outside valid operating range.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_STORE_READINESS
enum.description: Roll-up release-readiness state of a store.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_STORE_READINESS_NOT_READY
entry.description: Not ready to release (one or more blocking conditions).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_STORE_READINESS_READY
entry.description: All checks passed; cleared for release.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_STORE_READINESS_FAULT
entry.description: Store in fault state; must not be released.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_STORE_READINESS_RELEASED
entry.description: Store has been released from the carrier.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_TRACK_REL
enum.description: Relationship of a track to its parent, used when tracks split, merge, or are re-identified.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TRACK_REL_NONE
entry.description: No parent; this is an originating track.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TRACK_REL_CHILD
entry.description: Derived from a single parent track (e.g. a split).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TRACK_REL_MERGED
entry.description: Result of merging two or more parent tracks.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TRACK_REL_REID
entry.description: Re-identification of a previously dropped track.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_ID_METHOD
enum.description: Method by which a target identification was reached. Records the basis of ID, separate from classification.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ID_METHOD_GMTI
entry.description: Ground moving target indicator. Distinct from generic RADAR because it drives specific track-correlation handling in Link 16.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PID_STATUS
enum.description: Positive identification (PID) status of a target. Descriptive record, not a release authority.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PID_STATUS_TENTATIVE
entry.description: Tentative ID; PID not yet established.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_PID_STATUS_LOST
entry.description: PID previously held but since lost.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_ROE_STATE
enum.description: Rules-of-engagement / clearance state asserted for a target. Descriptive attestation carried for audit; does NOT gate weapon release.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ROE_STATE_CLEARED
entry.description: Engagement cleared by competent authority (attested, not commanded).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ROE_STATE_RESTRICTED
entry.description: Restricted: constraints apply (see no-strike / collateral context).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_NOSTRIKE_STATUS
enum.description: No-strike / restricted-target context for a coordinate or target.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_NOSTRIKE_STATUS_CLEAR
entry.description: Not on any no-strike or restricted list.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_NOSTRIKE_STATUS_NEAR
entry.description: Within proximity of a no-strike / protected entity.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_NOSTRIKE_STATUS_ON_LIST
entry.description: On a no-strike or restricted-target list.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE
enum.description: Engagement-control directive type. Provides abort / check-fire / re-target as first-class protocol actions alongside FIRES.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_RETARGET
entry.description: Re-target the referenced fire mission to a new track/coordinate.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_REQUESTED_EFFECT
enum.description: Coarse requested weapon effect, expressing requester INTENT (as in a call-for-fire method of engagement). The store controller translates this to device-internal fuze timing locally; this enum carries NO timing, height-of-burst, or arming-delay values and must not be extended to.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_REQUESTED_EFFECT_UNSPECIFIED
entry.description: No specific effect requested; store default.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_FUNCTIONAL_DAMAGE
enum.description: Discrete functional damage state for BDA (functional damage assessment layer, per CJCSI 3162.02 / JP 3-09), mirroring joint reporting. Carried alongside destruction_pct and the physical damage state, not replacing them.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FUNCTIONAL_DAMAGE_MISSION
entry.description: Mission kill (cannot perform role short of total destruction).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PHYSICAL_DAMAGE
enum.description: Discrete physical damage state for BDA (physical damage assessment layer, per CJCSI 3162.02A Methodology for Combat Assessment). Distinct from the functional-kill layer.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_STANAG_IDENTITY
enum.description: Standard identity of a track, aligned to MIL-STD-2525D / APP-6D standard identity (SIDC digit 4). MIL-STD-2525D is Distribution A, making it a public authoritative source. Richer than MAVLINK_M_TARGET_FORCE: preserves PENDING / ASSUMED_FRIEND / SUSPECT distinctions that carry ROE meaning and are lost if collapsed to FRIENDLY/FOE. Values follow the 2525D digit-4 code so a gateway can populate a SIDC directly.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SIDC_CONTEXT
enum.description: Reality context of a track, per MIL-STD-2525D SIDC digit 3. Lets exercise/simulation tracks be distinguished from real ones.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_ENVIRONMENT
enum.description: Track environment / dimension, aligned to the STANAG 5516 / APP-6 battle dimension. Pairs with MAVLINK_M_STANAG_IDENTITY to make a track mappable to joint symbology. Value numbering to be confirmed against spec.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_TRACK_NUMBER_TYPE
enum.description: Type/namespace of the external track number carried alongside the native track_uid, so a gateway knows how to interpret it. Encodings per the respective standard; do not assume a format from this enum alone.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_PPLI_TYPE
enum.description: Nature of a participant reporting its own position/identity (PPLI-style). Value numbering to be confirmed against spec.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MUNITION_GUIDANCE
enum.description: Coarse guidance category of a loaded munition. Descriptive inventory data, not employment configuration.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MUNITION_WARHEAD
enum.description: Coarse warhead category of a loaded munition. Descriptive inventory data; mirrors the effect families used by MAVLINK_M_SPLASH_FUNCTION. Not employment configuration.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_FUZE_HEALTH
enum.description: Coarse HEALTH of the fuze subsystem. This reports whether the fuze is functioning, NOT how it is configured. Fuze mode/timing/height-of-burst configuration is intentionally out of scope for this dialect and is device-internal.

enum.name: MAV_CMD
enum.description: MAVLink-M store-handling commands. Sent via COMMAND_LONG/COMMAND_INT; responses via COMMAND_ACK.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_MAVLINK_M_STORE_ARM
entry.description: Safe a store's payload. A command carries no time_usec, so no stop can be ordered against an arm sent this way (SAFETY BOUNDARIES): receivers answer an arm (Arm = 1) with MAV_RESULT_DENIED, and PAYLOAD_CONTROL arms. Gate: STORE_STATUS.release_consent = 1 is required for an arm on the targeted bay; a disarm is always accepted.
entry.param: Target store instance (0 = every store on the receiving system).
0 = safe/disarm. 1 = arm, which receivers deny; arm with PAYLOAD_CONTROL.
Ignored: a safe applies whatever the payload challenge holds, as a PAYLOAD_CONTROL DISARM does.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_MAVLINK_M_STORE_RUN_BIT
entry.description: Run a built-in self-test (BIT) on a store. Never sent with target_system 0; receivers ignore one that is.
entry.param: Target store instance (0 = every store on the receiving system).

entry.name: MAV_CMD_MAVLINK_M_STORE_REQUEST_STATUS
entry.description: Request status push from a store.
entry.param: Target store instance (0 = every store on the receiving system).
0 = STORE_STATUS only, 1 = all STORE_SENSOR_STATUS plus PAYLOAD_SENSOR_STATUS, 2 = both.

entry.name: MAV_CMD_MAVLINK_M_STORE_SET_DECEL_THRESHOLD
entry.description: Set the deceleration/landing-system trigger threshold for a store. Never sent with target_system 0; receivers ignore one that is.
entry.param: Target store instance (0 = every store on the receiving system).
Threshold value in the sensor's native units.
0 = trigger when reading falls below threshold, 1 = trigger when reading rises above threshold.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MISSION_TYPE

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MISSION_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TGT_LOC_UNSPECIFIED

entry.description: Not specified (default for an unset field).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TRAJECTORY_UNSPECIFIED
entry.description: Not specified (default for an unset field).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_FIRE_CONTROL_METHOD

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_FCM_UNSPECIFIED

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_CDE_LEVEL
enum.description: Collateral-damage-estimation LEVEL NUMBER only (CJCSI 3160.01 series). Carries the level as a status value; NEVER the underlying CDE computation or population data.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_DMPI_REFERENCE_KIND
enum.description: How a desired-mean-point-of-impact reference is expressed. A precise mensurated DMPI tied to a weapon solution is treated as controlled and is NOT carried here; carry target location + TLE category instead.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_DMPI_TARGET_LOCATION
entry.description: DMPI = the target location already carried (with TLE category).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_DMPI_OFFSET_REF
entry.description: DMPI expressed as a labeled offset reference (not a mensurated coordinate).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_ATR_CONFIDENCE
enum.description: OPTIONAL, ADVISORY coarse tier for human display only, derived from the raw atr_confidence_pct. It has NO protocol-defined probability band and MUST NOT be used as an automated rules-of-engagement input; the raw score + model id are the authoritative fields and the C2 node owns the threshold policy.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ATR_CONF_NA
entry.description: Not an ATR identification / not applicable.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ATR_CONF_LOW
entry.description: Advisory display tier: low. No protocol-defined band.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ATR_CONF_MEDIUM
entry.description: Advisory display tier: medium. No protocol-defined band.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_ATR_CONF_HIGH
entry.description: Advisory display tier: high. No protocol-defined band.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_LM_CONSENT_STATE
enum.description: Man-in-the-loop consent-to-strike state for a loitering munition / OWA UAS. HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP INSTRUMENT: this records a human consent decision and its withdrawal. It MUST NOT be used to construct an automated release path; release authority remains with the crewed C2 system, and consent is a precondition recorded for accountability, not a trigger.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE
enum.description: Loitering-munition abort / terminate action.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE_WAVE_OFF
entry.description: Wave off / break engagement, remain flyable.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE_ABORT
entry.description: Abort current attack, return to loiter.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_TST_STATUS
enum.description: Time-sensitive-target prosecution status.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MUNITION_FAMILY
enum.description: Munition family (composite munition, part 1 of 3). Descriptive class names, all Distribution-A doctrine.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_DPICM
entry.description: Dual-purpose ICM (e.g. M483A1). Distinct submunition/dispersion profile from APICM.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_APICM
entry.description: Antipersonnel ICM (e.g. M449 family). Distinct dispersion from DPICM.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_SCATTERABLE_MINE
entry.description: Scatterable mine (RAAMS/ADAM); carries SD-duration enum, not exact seconds.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_SENSOR_FUZED
entry.description: Sensor-fused / top-attack (SADARM, BONUS). Requires aimpoint-offset footprint, not a point coordinate.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_PRECISION
entry.description: Precision/guided conventional (Excalibur). Requires 10-digit grid + TLE minimum.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_PGK
entry.description: Precision guidance kit / APMI. Hybrid HE/PGM; TLE minimum required or reverts ballistic.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_THERMOBARIC
entry.description: Thermobaric / fuel-air explosive. Overpressure-primary; hardened/subterranean targets.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_MUN_FAM_LOITERING
entry.description: Loitering munition / LMAMS. Platform becomes terminal-guidance/relay, not passive observer.

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_MUNITION_PAYLOAD
enum.description: Munition payload (composite munition, part 3 of 3).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_WARHEAD_MODE
enum.description: Coarse selectable warhead MODE for a multi-mode / selectable warhead (e.g. a penetrating warhead with a surface-vs-penetrate selection on a multi-drop magazine). Reports/sets the coarse mode only. This is a SAFE/ARM-adjacent coarse selection, NOT a fuze timing channel: it must never be widened to carry an inter-stage delay or any timing value. The actual timing (e.g. secondary-charge delay) is device-internal and is configured on the component bus (DroneCAN or vendor structure) below the FMU, never on this dialect.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_WARHEAD_MODE_UNSPECIFIED
entry.description: Not specified / not a selectable warhead.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_WARHEAD_MODE_AIRBURST
entry.description: Airburst / height-of-burst effect selected (coarse selection; no HOB value carried).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SD_DURATION
enum.description: Scatterable-mine self-destruct duration CATEGORY (not exact seconds).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_EFFECT_VERB
enum.description: Mission-effect task verb (FM 3-09 / ATP 3-60), SEPARATE from burst geometry. The verb is descriptive tasking intent. The doctrinal casualty-percentage definitions are NOT carried on the wire (they drift from tasking intent to effects computation).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_MODE
enum.description: Commanded/reported sensor payload mode (UCI-style tasking).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_MODE_LASER_DESIGNATE
entry.description: Laser designation (code carried as slot elsewhere, not a value).

enum.name: MAVLINK_M_TASKING_STATUS
enum.description: Response to an inbound tasking request (UCI publish/subscribe event).

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TASKING_UNSPECIFIED
entry.description: Marks a SENSOR_TASKING request; a status response never carries it. Not an acceptance.

entry.name: MAVLINK_M_TASKING_INTERRUPTED
entry.description: Tasking ended before completion for a reason its requester did not cause: another request took the sensor, or the sensor lost the track it was following. Sent to the requester of the interrupted task.

Target longitude, WGS84.

Identifier of the assigned effector.

SURFACE and OBSCURATION are supplementary sensor context.

message.name: PAYLOAD_STATE
message.description: Telemetry for one fitted payload: capability, class, sequential lifecycle state, condition flags, and the state-bound auxiliary datum. Replaces ESAD_STATE, whose arming / munition / ignition state triad and fault flags are absorbed into payload_state and status_flags. payload_id identifies the payload instance (operator / C2 perception); store_id identifies the physical bay (carrier perception). payload_id = 0 reports the unfit slot itself; a consumer that knows only this dialect file can interpret every field, including the class-banded meanings, from payload_class plus the payload enums (a 3014 CLASS CODE + DESCRIPTOR resolution).
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Payload instance id, assigned by the operator / C2. 0 = no payload fitted in this store (reporting the slot's state). 1-254 = fitted instance. 255 = reserved.

Store instance identifier. Fixed physical bay assignment: a bay keeps its store_id permanently, and when a store is expended the bay may be reloaded under the same store_id. IDs never renumber. 0 = not applicable / single store. This is the canonical definition of store_id across the dialect.

Challenge hash (128 bits, little-endian) for this payload instance, which a PAYLOAD_CONTROL or PAYLOAD_CONFIG must carry. It ties a command to this state and is not secret. Receivers compare it byte-for-byte; all-zero if no payload is fitted.
Reported payload capability (what the device does; e.g. command, proximity, semi-auto). NONE if not yet established.

Function class of the fitted device (ESAD / gun / non-lethal / loitering / other). Lets a consumer interpret the class-banded sensor types and auxiliary meanings normative for this payload without a side table. MUST be non-UNKNOWN whenever a class-banded field is present. UNKNOWN if not yet established.
Reported lifecycle state (sequential, mutually exclusive).

Condition flags (bitmask, multiple may be set): busy, subsystem fault, internal fault, service request, sensor-gated, fired. Distinct from payload_aux: flags say which conditions hold, the aux carries the state-bound detail.

State-bound auxiliary datum: at most one at a time, meaning defined by the payload_state it is reported with (e.g. remaining safe-separation seconds while in SST, error descriptor while in ERROR). "0" / empty if none. Opaque to a receiver except where the state entry names its meaning; display other values verbatim.

Track UID (UUID) of the engagement this store is armed for, when applicable. Ties the armed state to a specific authorized track. All-zero if not associated with a track, and cleared to all-zero when the store is disarmed.

message.name: PAYLOAD_CONTROL
message.description: Payload control command requesting a state change (or mode change) on one or more payload instances on the receiving system. An ARM or ACTIVATE must carry the challenge the selected payload advertises in PAYLOAD_STATE; with payload_id = 0 it applies only if every local payload selected by store_id advertises that hash, and is otherwise rejected, so an ARM never applies in part. A DISARM or DEACTIVATE applies to every selected local payload without checking the challenge hash, so no payload's state can block it; as for any stop, MAVLink message signing on the link authenticates the sender. An addressed ARM or ACTIVATE whose payload_id and store_id select no local payload is rejected, and an addressed DISARM that selects none is answered MAVLINK_M_ACK_NOT_APPLICABLE; a DISARM sent to every system that selects no local payload is not acted on or answered. Each system judges only its own payloads, so a command that reaches several systems can apply on some and not on others; the originator confirms the result for each system from its MAVLINK_M_ACK and PAYLOAD_STATE. ARM and ACTIVATE additionally require the carrier's release consent (STORE_STATUS.release_consent = 1) on each targeted bay.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).

System ID of the intended recipient. 0 (every system) is valid only for MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATE_CHANGE_REQUEST_DISARM and MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_STATE_CHANGE_REQUEST_DEACTIVATE, which each receiving system applies to its own payloads; receivers ignore an arm or activate request sent with 0.
Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.
Target payload instance. 0 = all instances selected by store_id. 1-254 = specific instance. 255 = reserved.
Target store instance. 0 = all stores on the receiving system.

Challenge hash (128 bits, little-endian) the selected payload advertises in PAYLOAD_STATE. Checked for ARM / ACTIVATE, where with payload_id = 0 every selected local payload must advertise it; not checked for a DISARM or DEACTIVATE.
Requested state change (none, disarm, arm, mode, activate, deactivate).
Requested mode / function change (command, proximity, semi-auto, auto). Interpreted only when state_change = MODE; NONE otherwise.
Track UID (see TRACK_IDENTITY) of the engagement an ARM is for, reported back in PAYLOAD_STATE.track_uid. All-zero if the arming is not tied to a track. Ignored for DISARM.

message.name: PAYLOAD_CONFIG
message.description: Authenticated PARTIAL settings update for a fitted payload: only the setting(s) actually changing are carried (update_count config_type/config_value pairs and optionally config_name), never the full settings table, so a one-field change is a short message. Checked the same way as a PAYLOAD_CONTROL command: the payload_challenge_hash must match the value the selected payload last advertised in PAYLOAD_STATE, so a command made for an older state does not apply. The hash is public, since PAYLOAD_STATE goes to every system; MAVLink message signing on the link authenticates the sender. With payload_id = 0 and/or store_id = 0, a receiving system applies the configuration only if every local payload selected advertises the payload_challenge_hash, and otherwise rejects it. A command that selects no local payload is rejected. Numeric pairs are category-native (WEIGHT in grams; PAYLOAD_ID / STORE_ID as numeric ids); the assigned name travels in config_name. Only coarse, device-defined settings may be set here; this message must never carry a free continuous distance, a fuze timing value, or any height-of-burst configuration. The carrier's authoritative table is reported by PAYLOAD_SETTINGS.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
System ID of the intended recipient. Never 0; receivers ignore a PAYLOAD_CONFIG sent to every system.
Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.
Target payload instance to configure. 0 = all instances selected by store_id. 1-254 = specific instance. 255 = reserved.
Target store instance. 0 = all stores on the receiving system.
Challenge hash (128 bits, little-endian) the selected payload advertises in PAYLOAD_STATE. With payload_id = 0 or store_id = 0, every selected local payload must advertise this hash.
Number of valid config_type/config_value pairs (0-4). 0 = name-only update.
Category of each pair; slots at and past update_count MUST be NONE.
Category-native value per pair, little-endian (WEIGHT in grams; PAYLOAD_ID / STORE_ID as numeric id). 0 = padding slot.
Newly assigned payload name (null-terminated). Empty = name unchanged.

message.name: RWS_POSE
message.description: Remote Weapon System (RWS) pose relative to the host vehicle. Describes the physical mounting offset and orientation of the weapon system, plus its absolute position and velocity if available.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
RWS latitude, WGS84. INT32_MAX if unknown.
RWS longitude, WGS84. INT32_MAX if unknown.
RWS altitude, MSL. NaN if unknown.
Velocity north component (NED). NaN if unknown.
Velocity east component (NED). NaN if unknown.
Velocity down component (NED). NaN if unknown.
Position covariance, north axis (m^2). NaN if unknown.
Position covariance, east axis (m^2). NaN if unknown.
Position covariance, down axis (m^2). NaN if unknown.
Velocity covariance, north axis (m^2/s^2). NaN if unknown.
Velocity covariance, east axis (m^2/s^2). NaN if unknown.
Velocity covariance, down axis (m^2/s^2). NaN if unknown.
Mounting offset X from vehicle reference point in coordinate_frame.
Mounting offset Y from vehicle reference point in coordinate_frame.
Mounting offset Z from vehicle reference point in coordinate_frame.
RWS orientation quaternion [w, x, y, z] relative to coordinate_frame.
Roll orientation accuracy (1-sigma).
Pitch orientation accuracy (1-sigma).
Yaw orientation accuracy (1-sigma).
Coordinate frame for offset and orientation. See MAV_FRAME.

message.name: RWS_STATE
message.description: Remote Weapon System (RWS) operational state including arming status and loaded weapon information.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Human-readable weapon description or designation (null-terminated).
Current arming state of the weapon system.
Weapon type identifier (implementation-defined).

message.name: SENSOR_TASKING
message.description:
Inbound sensor/payload tasking from a UCI C2 node, and the platform's tasking-status response. Provided for gateway mapping between UCI publish/subscribe events and native MAVLink payload control; it does not replace MAVLink platform control. Carries commanded sensor mode and an optional point of interest or track to slew to.
A request carries status MAVLINK_M_TASKING_UNSPECIFIED and is addressed to the sensor or payload. A status response carries any other status and is addressed to the requester: the source system and component IDs in the request's frame header. A response echoes task_id and track_uid and reports the mode in effect in sensor_mode; receivers ignore its point-of-interest fields. When a task ends for any reason other than its requester's own request, the sensor sends that requester a status response with MAVLINK_M_TASKING_INTERRUPTED, echoing the task's task_id and track_uid. Status responses go only to the requester.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).

System ID of the intended recipient: the sensor's system for a request, the requester's for a status response. Never 0, not even to cage every sensor: a STANDBY sent to every system would also cage a designator guiding a weapon already in flight. Receivers ignore a SENSOR_TASKING sent with 0.

Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system: the sensor or payload for a request, the requester for a status response. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.

Tasking correlation id, chosen by the requester and echoed unchanged in every status response for that task. A sensor tells tasks apart by the requester's system and component IDs together with task_id.
Commanded sensor/payload mode in a request; the mode in effect in a status response.
MAVLINK_M_TASKING_UNSPECIFIED in a request, any other value in a status response; this is how a receiver tells the two apart.
Point-of-interest latitude to slew to, WGS84. INT32_MAX = not provided (0 is a valid coordinate).
Point-of-interest longitude to slew to, WGS84. INT32_MAX = not provided (0 is a valid coordinate).
Point-of-interest altitude, MSL. NaN = not provided.

Track UID (see TRACK_IDENTITY) the sensor is to follow. When set, the sensor follows that track and the point of interest is only a starting cue; with sensor_mode MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_MODE_LASER_DESIGNATE or MAVLINK_M_SENSOR_MODE_IR_MARK the track only cues the sensor, which lases or marks what its own tracker holds. All-zero to point at the point of interest.

message.name: CAS_9LINE
message.description: Close air support 9-line brief (JP 3-09.3 / JFIRE). Descriptive tasking data classes for a CAS attack. Laser code is carried as a slot, never a value. Danger close is a flag; RED tables are never embedded.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
System ID of the intended recipient: the attacking aircraft. A flight gets the brief addressed to each of its aircraft. Never 0; receivers ignore a 9-line sent to every system.
Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.
Engagement sequence of this brief, chosen by its sender. TERMINAL_CONTROL.sequence refers to it. 0xFFFF is reserved: in a stop it means every brief.
Line 1: initial point / battle position latitude, WGS84.
Line 1: initial point / battle position longitude, WGS84.
Line 2: heading (IP to target).
Line 2: offset (L/R); sign indicates side.
Line 3: distance IP to target.
Line 4: target elevation, MSL.
Line 6: target latitude, WGS84.
Line 6: target longitude, WGS84.
Line 7: type of mark / terminal guidance.
Line 7: 1 = a laser code is assigned (slot); 0 = none. Never the numeric code.
Line 8: friendlies latitude, WGS84.
Line 8: friendlies longitude, WGS84.
Line 9: egress heading.
Remarks: final attack heading (FAH). 0xFFFF if unspecified.
Remarks: 1 = danger close / troops in contact; 0 = not.
Bomb-on-coordinate vs bomb-on-target.
Track UID (see TRACK_IDENTITY) of the target this brief describes. All-zero if not associated with a track.

message.name: TERMINAL_CONTROL
message.description: Terminal-attack-control handshake (JP 3-09.3). Carries the control type, the clearance or abort verb, and attacking-aircraft status calls. Both ends send it. The controller sends clearance, addressed to the attacking aircraft, with aircraft_call MAVLINK_M_ACFT_CALL_NONE. The aircraft sends aircraft_call, addressed to the controller (the source of the CAS_9LINE with this sequence), with clearance MAVLINK_M_CAS_NONE, so a report is never read as a clearance or an abort. MAVLINK_M_CAS_CONTINUE and MAVLINK_M_CAS_CLEARED_HOT are human-authority instruments: they record a human decision, must not be wired as an automated release path, and are acted on only from the controller that sent the brief. MAVLINK_M_CAS_ABORT and MAVLINK_M_CAS_CEASE_FIRE are safety actions: the aircraft acts on them on receipt from any sender, whatever tac_type and abort_authority_present say.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).

System ID of the intended recipient: the attacking aircraft for a clearance, the controller for an aircraft call. 0 (every system) is valid only with clearance MAVLINK_M_CAS_ABORT or MAVLINK_M_CAS_CEASE_FIRE, and a receiver acts only on that clearance in such a message; receivers ignore any other TERMINAL_CONTROL sent with 0.
Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.

Engagement sequence this handshake applies to: the CAS_9LINE.sequence of the brief it controls. With clearance MAVLINK_M_CAS_ABORT or MAVLINK_M_CAS_CEASE_FIRE, 0xFFFF means every attack the receiving aircraft is making.
Type of terminal attack control (1/2/3).
Clearance / abort verb (human authority).
Attacking-aircraft status call.
1 = a valid abort authority is established for this engagement; 0 = not. A precondition for MAVLINK_M_CAS_CLEARED_HOT; it never gates MAVLINK_M_CAS_ABORT or MAVLINK_M_CAS_CEASE_FIRE.

message.name: TARGET_CUE
message.description:
Non-kinetic point-of-interest cue relayed from a sensing/ISR platform to one or more consumers (e.g. a manually piloted aircraft, an OSD, or a GCS) to direct attention to a WGS84 location for observation or investigation. Carries the geolocated point and minimal context only. It intentionally omits the authorization token, weaponeering, and CEP fields of the fires-related messages so that ISR cueing is cleanly separable from engagement on the wire.
Bearing and range to the cue are NOT transmitted: a consumer computes them locally from this point and its own GLOBAL_POSITION_INT, so the same cue is valid for every receiver regardless of position.
target_class and target_force on a cue are the SENSING platform's provisional read at detection, qualified by confidence_score - a starting hint, NOT an established identification. A cue does not identify or authorize; identification is carried on TRACK_IDENTITY and the engagement decision on TARGET_AUTHORIZATION. A consumer must not treat a cued class or affiliation as confirmed, and must never derive a release decision from a cue.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Unique identifier of this cue, assigned by the originator.
Parent target set identifier, if associated. 0 = none.
Cue latitude, WGS84.
Cue longitude, WGS84.
Cue altitude, MSL. NaN if unknown.
Velocity north (NED) if the point is moving. NaN if unknown/static.
Velocity east (NED) if the point is moving. NaN if unknown/static.
Velocity down (NED) if the point is moving. NaN if unknown/static.
Confidence of the geolocation and of the provisional class/force read [0.0-1.0]. NaN if not provided.
MAVLink system ID of the originating (sensing) platform.
Intent of the cue. Non-kinetic.
Provisional target classification from the sensing platform, qualified by confidence_score. A hint, not an identification.
Provisional force affiliation from the sensing platform, qualified by confidence_score. A hint, not a combat-ID determination; do not use as a release input.
Short human-readable label (null-terminated).

message.name: MAVLINK_M_ACK
message.description:
Generic acknowledgment for MAVLink-M messages. A recipient emits this in response to an acknowledged MAVLink-M message to close the loop on delivery and acceptance, addressed to the system and component that sent that message. Keyed by the acknowledged message ID, an instance identifier (e.g. cue_id, target_set_id, or sequence) and that message's time_usec, so the originator can match the ACK to the one message it answers. The acknowledging system identifies itself in the MAVLink frame header.
Every MAVLink-M message that carries target_system is acknowledged, except SENSOR_TASKING, which its status response answers. The recipient answers with one final result, and may send MAVLINK_M_ACK_RECEIVED first while a human decision is pending. A message sent with target_system 0 is answered only by the systems where it selects something, with the result of applying it there, each after a short random delay so that answers on a shared channel do not collide. A system where it selects nothing, or that does not support it, does not answer, so a stop sent to every system draws one acknowledgment from each system it stops rather than one from every system on the network, and its sender expects answers only from the systems it knows hold what the stop selects. A sender with a start of its own still unacknowledged by a system also addresses the stop to that system, so that system answers it whether or not the start has arrived. Silence cannot show that a stop reached a holder its sender did not know of, so a sender that cannot rule one out repeats the stop unchanged a number of times set for the network, an answer timeout apart, and stops repeating once it issues a start the stop covers. A sender that gets no acknowledgment from a system it expects to answer sends the stop again addressed to that system, up to that number of times, and may send any other message again, unchanged, time_usec included. A receiver treats a repeat of a message it has processed (same source system and component, message ID and field values, target_system and target_component aside) as a duplicate: it does not act on it a second time, and answers it with its latest answer to that message, or with MAVLINK_M_ACK_NOT_APPLICABLE when it gave none and the repeat is addressed to it. Receivers ignore an acknowledgment sent with target_system 0.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).

time_usec of the acknowledged message, copied unchanged. Tells apart acknowledgments of different messages with the same ack_msgid and ack_instance, such as a MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_CHECK_FIRE and the MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_RESUME of the same mission.
System ID of the recipient: the source system ID in the frame header of the acknowledged message, not that message's own target_system. Never 0.
Component ID of the recipient: the source component ID in the frame header of the acknowledged message, not that message's own target_component. Never 0.
MAVLink message ID being acknowledged (e.g. 53001 for TARGET_CUE).
Instance identifier of the acknowledged item (e.g. cue_id / target_set_id / sequence). 0 if not applicable.
Result of receiving/processing the acknowledged message.
Optional human-readable reason, primarily for REJECTED/FAILED (null-terminated).

message.name: STORE_SENSOR_STATUS
message.description: Health and current reading of one deceleration/landing-trigger sensor on a store. Emitted per sensor (one message per sensor) so the set of sensors per store can vary. A pre-release consumer aggregates these into a go/no-go decision (see STORE_STATUS).
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Current sensor reading in the sensor's native units. NaN if invalid.
Lower bound of the valid operating range, native units. NaN if unspecified.
Upper bound of the valid operating range, native units. NaN if unspecified.
Store instance identifier this sensor belongs to.
Type of sensor (shared-band entries only on this carrier-side channel; class-banded entries belong on PAYLOAD_SENSOR_STATUS keyed to the fitted payload's class).
Index when multiple sensors of the same type exist on a store (0-based).
Health state of this sensor.
How value, value_min and value_max must be read (analog / count / discrete / text). Unknown if not reported.

message.name: STORE_STATUS
message.description: Per-store roll-up summary, carrier-side, for release decisions. Aggregates the fitted payload's lifecycle state (mirrored from the carrier's last received PAYLOAD_STATE for convenience) and deceleration-sensor health into a single readiness value, plus the carrier's release consent for the bay, so an operator/GCS can gate release without parsing every sensor message. release_consent is the carrier's authorization for this store to move into a hazardous state (PAYLOAD_CONTROL ARM / ACTIVATE). It mirrors the MIL-STD-1760 Release Consent discrete: a carrier-side state, scoped to a single bay, gating the move into hazardous states only - DISARM and DEACTIVATE always apply. It is not a payload-type clearance and not a release/drop authorization.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Bitmask of MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SENSOR_TYPE shared-band values currently NOT healthy (bit = 1<<sensor_type).
Store instance identifier.
Total number of stores on the carrier (lets the GCS know how many to expect). 0 if unknown.
Roll-up release-readiness state.
Lifecycle state of the fitted payload in this store (mirrored from the carrier's last received PAYLOAD_STATE for convenience). Re-pointed from the old ESAD arming state; wire-breaking.
Count of sensors reporting OK.
Total count of sensors on this store.
Carrier release consent for this store: 0 = not currently authorized for ARM/ACTIVATE on this bay, 1 = authorized (MIL-STD-1760 Release Consent analog). DISARM and DEACTIVATE are always accepted.

message.name: TRACK_IDENTITY
message.description:
Correlation spine for the kill chain. Binds one real-world object to a globally-unique track UID that persists across find, fix, track, target, engage, and assess, so every downstream report can be tied back to the same object. Carries the basis of identification (method + confidence) separately from classification, and lineage when tracks split or merge.
This message asserts identity and how it was derived. It does not assert engagement authority; see TARGET_AUTHORIZATION.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Globally-unique track identifier (UUID). Stable across the whole chain.
Parent track UID for split/merge/re-id lineage. All-zero if none.
Associated target set identifier, if any. 0 = none.
Time the object was first detected (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Confidence of identification [0.0-1.0]. NaN if not provided.
System ID of the platform that originated/owns this track.
Sensor/method underlying the current identification.
Method by which identification was reached.
Positive identification status (descriptive).
Relationship to parent track (split/merge/re-id).
Classification (what it is), distinct from id_method (how it was identified).
Force affiliation.
Optional free-text basis/notes for the identification (null-terminated).
External/joint track number (e.g. Link 16 track number or VMF URN), as text for gateway round-trip. Empty if none. Encoding per external_track_type.
Namespace of external_track_number.
STANAG/APP-6 standard identity (richer than target_force).
STANAG/APP-6 battle dimension / environment.
ATR model confidence [0-100]. 255 = N/A. Raw score; the C2 node owns any ROE threshold.
Identifier of the ATR model/version that produced atr_confidence_pct. 0 = unspecified.
OPTIONAL advisory display tier derived from atr_confidence_pct. Not for automated ROE.
Reality context (MIL-STD-2525D SIDC digit 3): real-world vs exercise vs simulation. Prevents a live track and an exercise/simulated track from being indistinguishable on a joint net.

message.name: TARGET_AUTHORIZATION
message.description:
Accountability attestation for a track. Records that a specific human authority asserted positive identification, an ROE/clearance state, and no-strike context at a specific time, so the decision trail travels with the chain and is auditable after the fact.
IMPORTANT: this message is a DESCRIPTIVE RECORD, not a command. It does NOT grant authority, does NOT gate or trigger weapon release, and must not be used as an arming or engagement interlock. Release authority lives in the crewed C2 system. A receiver must never treat the presence of this message as permission to act.
message.field: Timestamp this attestation was recorded (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Track UID this authorization record applies to.
Time the authority made the decision (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Expiry of this attestation (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC). 0 = unspecified.
Freshness nonce bound into the authorization token by the C2 node. A verifier caches seen nonces within the validity window to reject replays. Anti-replay input only; not itself a secret.
Collateral-damage estimate context [0.0-1.0 normalized], if assessed. NaN if not.
Opaque identifier of the authorizing authority/operator (for audit).
Opaque authorization token (carried for record; not a release key).
PID status asserted by the authority.
ROE/clearance state asserted (attested, not commanded).
No-strike / restricted-target context.
Human-readable role of the authority (e.g. designation), null-terminated.
Collateral-damage-estimation LEVEL number only (CJCSI 3160.01). Never the underlying computation or population data.

message.name: ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE
message.description:
Engagement-control directive making abort, check-fire, resume, and re-target first-class actions alongside FIRES. The ability to STOP a mission is a protocol citizen, not an afterthought. Should be paired with MAVLINK_M_ACK so the originator gets positive confirmation the directive was received and actioned.
MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_ABORT and MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_CHECK_FIRE are safety actions: every system they select acts on them on receipt, once message signing accepts them (see SAFETY BOUNDARIES). They do not require the authorization trail that initiating fire does.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).

System ID of the intended recipient. 0 (every system) is valid only for MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_ABORT and MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_CHECK_FIRE; receivers ignore any other directive sent with 0.
Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.

Track UID the directive applies to. All-zero if addressed by sequence only. A MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_ABORT or MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_CHECK_FIRE applies to every engagement that matches its sequence or its nonzero track_uid, whoever issued that engagement, and is never declined because one selector does not match. A MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_RESUME or MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_RETARGET applies only to an engagement that matches every selector it carries.

Fire mission sequence number the directive applies to. For MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_ABORT and MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_CHECK_FIRE, 0xFFFF means every fire mission the receiving system holds.
Effector the directive is addressed to. 0 = all assigned.
New target latitude for RETARGET, WGS84. INT32_MAX = not provided (0,0 is a valid coordinate). Ignored unless directive is RETARGET.
New target longitude for RETARGET, WGS84. INT32_MAX = not provided. Ignored unless directive is RETARGET.
New target altitude for RETARGET, MSL. NaN = not provided. Ignored unless directive is RETARGET.
Directive type.

System ID of the system that first issued the directive. A system that passes the directive on as a message of its own keeps this value, so it can differ from the source system ID in the frame header; routers never change either. Not authenticated: for display and audit, never a reason to act or not to act on the directive.

message.name: CALL_FOR_FIRE
message.description: Complete call-for-fire method elements (ATP 3-09.30 Ch.4; maps to VMF K02.4). Complements FIRES (which carries target + munition/fuze) with the warning-order, method-of-engagement, and method-of-fire-and-control elements a VMF/Link-16 packer requires. Descriptive intent only.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
System ID of the intended recipient: the fire direction center. Never 0; receivers ignore a call for fire sent to every system.
Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.
Fire-mission sequence number this CFF applies to.
Warning-order mission type.
Method of target location.
Area vs precision.
Low/high angle.
Distribution / sheaf.
Method of fire and control.
1 = danger close (target within doctrinal threshold of friendlies); 0 = not. Flag only, no RED table.
Number of rounds for fire for effect. 0 = unspecified.
Duration of fire. 0 = unspecified.
Target-location-error category label.
1 = coordinate mensurated from precision imagery; 0 = map spot.
Linear-target sheaf length (special sheaf). 0 if N/A.
Linear-target sheaf width (special sheaf). 0 if N/A.
Linear-target sheaf attitude (special sheaf), centidegrees [0..35999]. 0xFFFF = N/A (0 is a valid attitude, due north).

Virtual observer-target direction (bearing observer/drone to target), centidegrees [0..35999]. Lets the gateway orient VMF K02.22 relative corrections (Add/Drop, L/R) from an absolute-coordinate edge feed. 0xFFFF = not provided (0 is a valid bearing, due north).
Observer-target factor: OT range / 1000, in decimeters of shift per mil. Supports relative-correction math at the gateway. 0xFFFF = not provided.
Mission-effect task verb (suppress/neutralize/destroy/...), descriptive tasking intent. Distinct from mission_type and from the fuze-effect intent carried on FIRES.requested_effect.
Globally-unique track identifier (UUID) of the TRACK_IDENTITY this message correlates to. Ties the engagement/assessment to the authorized track. All-zero if not associated.

message.name: PARTICIPANT_POSITION
message.description:
Friendly-participant self-report of identity and position (PPLI-style / Blue Force Tracking). Distinct from target/cue messages: this is a network participant reporting "I am here, this is who I am" for the common operational picture, mappable to Link 16 PPLI, VMF position reports, and Cursor-on-Target friendly events.
Structural placeholder for joint interop; identity/type value sets and any external track-number encoding are per STANAG 5516 / MIL-STD-6017, to be reconciled from spec.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Participant latitude, WGS84.
Participant longitude, WGS84.
Participant altitude, MSL. NaN if unknown.
Velocity north (NED). NaN if unknown.
Velocity east (NED). NaN if unknown.
Velocity down (NED). NaN if unknown.
Course over ground. NaN if unknown.
External/joint track number or URN for this participant. Empty if none.
Human-readable callsign/designation (null-terminated).
System ID of the reporting participant.
Namespace of external_track_number.
Standard identity (normally FRIEND for own-force PPLI).
Participant environment/type.

message.name: STORE_MUNITION
message.description: Descriptive munition inventory/status for a store, for mapping into a joint weapon-status report (e.g. at a JTAC/C2 interface). Reports WHAT is loaded so a gateway maps real data rather than synthesizing it; it does NOT carry fuze/employment configuration, which is device-internal and out of scope for this dialect. Keyed by store_id to correlate with PAYLOAD_STATE / STORE_STATUS. Low-rate: changes on load and on release.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Munition mass. NaN if unknown.
External/joint track or store reference for gateway correlation. Empty if none.
Munition nomenclature/designation (null-terminated).
Count of this munition remaining available on the store/carrier.
Store instance identifier.
Munition type code (implementation-defined; consistent with the payload_class reported on PAYLOAD_STATE for this store).
Coarse guidance category.
Coarse warhead category.
Lifecycle state of the fitted payload in this store (mirrored from PAYLOAD_STATE for convenience). Re-pointed from the old ESAD arming state; wire-breaking.
Coarse fuze HEALTH (functioning/fault), not fuze configuration.
Namespace of external_track_number.
Composite-munition family (finer than the warhead/guidance pair). Descriptive.
Composite-munition payload category. Descriptive.

Coarse selectable warhead MODE currently set for a selectable/multi-mode warhead (e.g. surface vs penetrate on a multi-drop magazine store). Reports the mode only. It is a COARSE enum and MUST NOT be widened to carry a fuze timing / inter-stage delay value; the actual timing is device-internal and configured on the component bus (e.g. DroneCAN) below the FMU.
Scatterable-mine self-destruct duration CATEGORY (not exact seconds), for mine payloads.

message.name: LOITER_MUNITION_CONTROL
message.description:
Loitering-munition / one-way-attack UAS control and consent handshake (JFIRE 2023). SAFETY-CRITICAL: consent_state records a MAN-IN-THE-LOOP human decision and MUST NOT be used to build an automated release path; release authority remains with the crewed C2 system. terminate provides abort/wave-off/self-destruct. Pairs with TARGET_AUTHORIZATION (record). A loitering munition also acts on ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE: MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_ABORT as MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE_ABORT, and MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_CHECK_FIRE as MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE_WAVE_OFF held until a MAVLINK_M_ENGAGEMENT_DIRECTIVE_RESUME. When the loitering munition is also fitted in a store, its payload telemetry (lifecycle state, condition flags, sensor status) flows through the PAYLOAD_* messages with payload_class = MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_CLASS_LOITERING; this family remains distinct because the consent handshake is load-bearing for the LOITERING class and not a generic attribute.
Both ends send it. A munition sends consent_state MAVLINK_M_LM_CONSENT_REQUESTED addressed to the human authority for the engagement: the source of the FIRES or addressed LOITER_MUNITION_CONTROL that tasked it against track_uid. It applies MAVLINK_M_LM_CONSENT_GRANTED only from that system, and every stop from any sender. consent_state and terminate carry changes, not a copy of state: a sender sets them only to make that change and otherwise sends MAVLINK_M_LM_CONSENT_NONE and MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE_NONE, which leave the munition's consent and action as they are.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).

System ID of the intended recipient: the munition, or the human authority for a consent request. 0 (every system) is valid only to stop. From a message sent with 0, a munition applies terminate MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE_WAVE_OFF or MAVLINK_M_LM_TERMINATE_ABORT and consent_state MAVLINK_M_LM_CONSENT_WITHHELD or MAVLINK_M_LM_CONSENT_WITHDRAWN, treats any other terminate or consent_state value as none, and ignores the loiter station and every other field, so after an ABORT it returns to the loiter station it already holds. It never drops the stop because the message carries something else. Receivers ignore a LOITER_MUNITION_CONTROL sent with 0 that carries no stop.
Component ID of the intended recipient within target_system. 0 = every component of that system. Ignored when target_system is 0.
128-bit track UID of the engaged object (see TRACK_IDENTITY).
Man-in-the-loop consent-to-strike state (recorded human decision, not a trigger).
Abort / wave-off / self-destruct action.
Time-sensitive-target prosecution status.
Positive-identification status gate (from TRACK_IDENTITY set).
Collateral-damage-estimate level gate (number only).
Loiter/orbit station latitude, WGS84. INT32_MAX = not provided (0 is a valid coordinate).
Loiter/orbit station longitude, WGS84. INT32_MAX = not provided (0 is a valid coordinate).
How the desired point of impact is referenced (no mensurated coordinate).

message.name: PAYLOAD_SETTINGS
message.description: Carrier-assigned settings for a stored slot: the carrier's bookkeeping view of what is fitted. Response to PAYLOAD_GET_SETTINGS (53038); the carrier fills the same scope (payload_id / store_id) as requested. Low-rate: changes on loading, unloading, or setting assignment. SST duration and activation distance appear here for AWARENESS ONLY: they are device-defined coarse detents set locally (physical switch or component bus) and are intentionally not configurable over this bus, per the dialect's safe/arm boundary rule (no free continuous distance / delay value on the wire). required_sensor_mask is the readiness RECIPE: the subset of sensor types that MUST be health = OK for this slot's release / function decision. A consumer may recompute go/no-go from PAYLOAD_SENSOR_STATUS and STORE_SENSOR_STATUS alone.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Payload instance in this scope (0 = unfitted slot).
Carrier slot these settings belong to.
Assigned payload name (null-terminated). Empty = unnamed.
Mass of the stored payload as recorded by the carrier. NaN if unassigned.
Configured safe-separation timer in effect on the device. 0 = device enforces none. Awareness only, not settable here.
Configured maximum activation distance in effect on the device (proximity-type payloads). 0 = device enforces none. Awareness only, not settable here.

Bitmask of MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SENSOR_TYPE values that must report health = OK for this slot's readiness decision. 0 = no sensor gate. Defines the go/no-go recipe so a consumer can recompute readiness from PAYLOAD_SENSOR_STATUS.
Active challenge hash for this slot (lets the requester authenticate subsequent control). All-zero if no payload is fitted.

message.name: PAYLOAD_GET_SETTINGS
message.description: Query the carrier for PAYLOAD_SETTINGS (53037) for the scope below; the carrier responds with the same payload_id / store_id scope. Read-only: allowed even with an all-zero challenge hash.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Scope: which payload's settings are needed (0 = any payload in the slot scope).
Scope: which carrier slot (0 = whole carrier).
Last known active challenge hash for the scope; all-zero if not yet authenticated (allowed for this read-only query).

message.name: PAYLOAD_SENSOR_STATUS
message.description: Per-sensor health and reading for one fitted payload. Payload-side channel, bounded: pulled by the carrier or a GCS, or emitted at a bounded rate by the payload. The payload's autonomous footprint stays at the one condition-flag channel on PAYLOAD_STATE (status_flags); per-sensor detail flows on this message. The sensor set is class-scoped: a class-band sensor_type entry is normative for the payload_class named on this message (the 3014 CLASS CODE + DESCRIPTOR model). The carrier-side counterpart (53034 STORE_SENSOR_STATUS) covers the carrier's own decel / gate sensors that gate release. The two messages are distinct channels; both draw from the same MAVLINK_M_PAYLOAD_SENSOR_TYPE registry.
message.field: Timestamp (UNIX epoch, microseconds UTC).
Current sensor reading in the sensor's native units. NaN if invalid.
Lower bound of the valid operating range, native units. NaN if unspecified.
Upper bound of the valid operating range, native units. NaN if unspecified.
Payload instance this sensor belongs to. 1-254 = fitted instance; 0 invalid here (the carrier-side message covers the slot).
Carrier slot containing the payload this sensor belongs to.
Function class of the payload. Resolves the meaning of class-banded sensor_type entries per the entry description. Unknown if not yet established.
Type of sensor (shared-band or class-band entries).
Index when multiple sensors of the same type exist on the payload (0-based).
Health state of this sensor.
How value, value_min and value_max must be read (analog / count / discrete / text). Unknown if not reported.
